From 2ec6cf9b742a5c18982861322fa5de6510f8f57e Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Tariq Toukan <tariqt@nvidia.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Jun 2022 21:21:10 +0300
Subject: [PATCH] net/mlx5e: kTLS, Fix build time constant test in RX

Use the correct constant (TLS_DRIVER_STATE_SIZE_RX) in the comparison
against the size of the private RX TLS driver context.

Fixes: 1182f3659357 ("net/mlx5e: kTLS, Add kTLS RX HW offload support")
Signed-off-by: Tariq Toukan <tariqt@nvidia.com>
Reviewed-by: Maxim Mikityanskiy <maximmi@nvidia.com>
Signed-off-by: Saeed Mahameed <saeedm@nvidia.com>

diff --git a/drivers/net/ethernet/mellanox/mlx5/core/en_accel/ktls_rx.c b/drivers/net/ethernet/mellanox/mlx5/core/en_accel/ktls_rx.c
index 0bb0633b7542..27483aa7be8a 100644
--- a/drivers/net/ethernet/mellanox/mlx5/core/en_accel/ktls_rx.c
+++ b/drivers/net/ethernet/mellanox/mlx5/core/en_accel/ktls_rx.c
@@ -231,8 +231,7 @@ mlx5e_set_ktls_rx_priv_ctx(struct tls_context *tls_ctx,
 	struct mlx5e_ktls_offload_context_rx **ctx =
 		__tls_driver_ctx(tls_ctx, TLS_OFFLOAD_CTX_DIR_RX);
 
-	BUILD_BUG_ON(sizeof(struct mlx5e_ktls_offload_context_rx *) >
-		     TLS_OFFLOAD_CONTEXT_SIZE_RX);
+	BUILD_BUG_ON(sizeof(priv_rx) > TLS_DRIVER_STATE_SIZE_RX);
 
 	*ctx = priv_rx;
 }
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/net/ethernet/mellanox/mlx5/core/en_accel/ktls_rx.c`**
   - The line that checks the size of the RX TLS driver context has been modified. 
   - The original comparison used `TLS_OFFLOAD_CONTEXT_SIZE_RX`, which was incorrect.
   - The updated line now correctly uses `TLS_DRIVER_STATE_SIZE_RX` for the comparison.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification in `ktls_rx.c` addresses a bug related to the build-time constant test for the RX TLS driver context. By changing the constant used in the size comparison, the patch ensures that the size of the private RX TLS driver context is correctly validated against the appropriate constant, thereby fixing the issue introduced in a previous commit (identified by the fix tag). This change is crucial for maintaining the integrity of the kTLS RX hardware offload support functionality.

Here is the commit message:
net/mlx5e: kTLS, Fix build time constant test in RX

Use the correct constant (TLS_DRIVER_STATE_SIZE_RX) in the comparison
against the size of the private RX TLS driver context.

Fixes: 1182f3659357 ("net/mlx5e: kTLS, Add kTLS RX HW offload support")
Signed-off-by: Tariq Toukan <tariqt@nvidia.com>
Reviewed-by: Maxim Mikityanskiy <maximmi@nvidia.com>
Signed-off-by: Saeed Mahameed <saeedm@nvidia.com>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by using an incorrect constant (`TLS_OFFLOAD_CONTEXT_SIZE_RX`) in the build-time check for the size of the private RX TLS driver context, which led to potential mismatches and incorrect behavior in the kTLS RX hardware offload support. The correct constant (`TLS_DRIVER_STATE_SIZE_RX`) should have been used to ensure proper validation of the context size.

Here is the patch:
 
 static void
 mlx5e_set_ktls_rx_priv_ctx(struct tls_context *tls_ctx,
 			   struct mlx5e_ktls_offload_context_rx *priv_rx)
 {
 	struct mlx5e_ktls_offload_context_rx **ctx =
 		__tls_driver_ctx(tls_ctx, TLS_OFFLOAD_CTX_DIR_RX);
 
-	BUILD_BUG_ON(sizeof(struct mlx5e_ktls_offload_context_rx *) >
-		     TLS_OFFLOAD_CONTEXT_SIZE_RX);
+	BUILD_BUG_ON(sizeof(priv_rx) > TLS_DRIVER_STATE_SIZE_RX);
 
 	*ctx = priv_rx;
 }

```c
             TLS_OFFLOAD_CONTEXT_SIZE_RX);
```
Reason:
The bug occurs because the incorrect constant `TLS_OFFLOAD_CONTEXT_SIZE_RX` is used in the build-time check, which may not accurately reflect the size of the private RX TLS driver context. This can lead to mismatches in size validation, potentially causing incorrect behavior in the kTLS RX hardware offload support.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
BUILD_BUG_ON(sizeof(priv_rx) > TLS_DRIVER_STATE_SIZE_RX);
```
Reason:
The fix replaces the incorrect constant with the correct one, `TLS_DRIVER_STATE_SIZE_RX`, ensuring that the size of the private RX TLS driver context is properly validated. This change prevents potential mismatches and ensures the correct functioning of the kTLS RX hardware offload support.
